title: k-NN as an implementation of situation testing for discrimination discovery and prevention
abstract: With the support of the legally-grounded methodology of situation testing, we tackle the problems of discrimination discovery and prevention from a dataset of historical decisions by adopting a variant of k-NN classification. A tuple is labeled as discriminated if we can observe a significant difference of treatment among its neighbors belonging to a protected-by-law group and its neighbors not belonging to it. Discrimination discovery boils down to extracting a classification model from the labeled tuples. Discrimination prevention is tackled by changing the decision value for tuples labeled as discriminated before training a classifier. The approach of this paper overcomes legal weaknesses and technical limitations of existing proposals.

claims.text: A variant of k-NN classification can implement the methodology of situation testing for discrimination discovery and prevention in historical decision datasets.
A tuple is labeled as discriminated if a significant difference of treatment is observed between its neighbors belonging to a protected group and those not belonging to it.
Discrimination discovery is performed by extracting a classification model from tuples labeled as discriminated.
Discrimination prevention is performed by changing the decision value for tuples labeled as discriminated prior to classifier training.

limitations.text: Existing proposals for discrimination discovery and prevention suffer from legal weaknesses and technical limitations.

methodologies.name: k-NN situation testing variant
methodologies.description: A classification methodology that identifies discrimination by comparing treatment differences among k-NN neighbors in protected versus unprotected groups, and prevents discrimination by altering labels prior to classifier training.
